betting_tree_per_deal.measured: full betting-tree walk with one sampled runout per chance node, 5.0 s

public_tree_estimate.note: each public node carries 1,326-hand range vectors per player; a vector best-response pass is ~1e3-1e6 ops per node (hand-strength sort + prefix sums at terminals)

conclusions.exact_best_response_real_game: INFEASIBLE here: ~6.5e11 river public nodes even with suit isomorphism (>=1e15 ops); needs a C++/GPU vector BR and days of cluster time
conclusions.abstract_best_response: NOT MEANINGFUL / NOT COMPUTED: the v2 abstraction is imperfect-recall; a best response inside an imperfect-recall abstraction is not a well-defined game value and finding one is NP-hard in general
conclusions.exact_best_response_subgames: DONE: fixed-runout flop/turn subgames (Phases 56-57) and 52-card river subgames (Phase 34) give exact exploitability of the abstraction on those subgames
conclusions.local_best_response: FEASIBLE, NOT IMPLEMENTED: LBR (Lisy & Bowling 2017) gives a sampled LOWER bound on real-game exploitability. Estimated 1-5 s per hand in this Python code base (range tracking through the abstract strategy for 1,326 combos per opponent action, equity vs range for each LBR decision); 10,000 hands ~3-14 CPU-hours per strategy, SE ~0.1 BB/hand. Recommended as the next solver-quality measurement.

decision: no exact BR attempted; LBR recorded as the recommended future measurement; no gate or strategy change
